notes: The owner can now ask the product to forget a source, and the product says what that will do before it does it. The console's memory view lists every entry with the channel it arrived through and its short opaque id, and offers a forget action per entry. The action opens a confirmation that first shows a read-only preview - how many entries the forget would filter, and whether prompt injection, the memory view and the owner profile coverage are affected - and the confirm button stays disabled until that preview has arrived, so the consequence is always visible before anything is written. Cancelling writes nothing. The write is gated like every other console write and it records a tombstone: nothing is deleted, the entry stays in its file, and the read paths drop it from the next request on with no restart. The preview carries no entry text, no file path and no credential, and the slot is resolved through the active profile's own seams, so a named profile never addresses the repository's memory files. The limits are stated where they apply: a source that exists only in a session transcript still cannot be suppressed, a forget acts on one store at a time, and a restore of a backup taken before the forget into a machine with no ledger still brings the source back - the console now says so instead of implying otherwise. The counts move with the feature: 2896 core assertions and 1861 locale keys per pack, with two new gates for the flow. No new credential, no new outbound path, no change to any shared gateway.
